stem: Why is it generally recommended to tick the box for using a spacer on a pediatric asthma action plan?

options.text: Spacers ensure better delivery of the medication to the lungs in children
Spacers are only necessary if the child is using a dry powder inhaler
Using a spacer is the only way to measure peak flow accurately
It reduces the amount of medication needed to achieve the same effect

explanation: Spacers help overcome coordination issues, ensuring the inhaled medication reaches the lower airways effectively rather than hitting the back of the throat.
rationale: Think about the mechanical challenges young children face when trying to coordinate their breathing with a puffer.

optionExplanations.A: Spacers help overcome coordination issues, ensuring the inhaled medication reaches the lower airways effectively rather than hitting the back of the throat.
optionExplanations.B: Spacers are used with pressurized metered-dose inhalers (puffers), whereas dry powder inhalers typically do not use them.
optionExplanations.C: Peak flow meters are separate diagnostic tools and are not used in conjunction with a spacer for medication delivery.
optionExplanations.D: The dose remains the same, but the delivery efficiency is improved, ensuring the prescribed dose actually reaches the target area.
